RULING D38, COMMITTED VERBATIM: 'Ruling D38 (advisor, 2026-09-30; default chosen by the owner) — the deliberation watchdog finishes cleanly. A run with a declared time budget ends by its own terminal, never by being killed from outside mid-call. Slow deliberation is not itself a fault: no call is cancelled for being slow while the budget holds. Before each model call, if this run's own measured pace for that call's tier says the call cannot finish inside the remaining budget less a reserve for writing the terminal, the call is not started; during each call, when that point arrives, the call is cancelled. Either way the run ends at once with status blocked and a typed watchdog record naming the rule that fired, the node, iteration, tier, configured serving, elapsed time, budget and pace. Everything produced so far is kept. The terminal points at the last implementation the build judges agreed on and names which later gates it did or did not pass; the latest implementation, if it differs, is labelled unjudged (D22). A call that runs far past its tier's pace in this run is flagged in the record, not cancelled, until measured runs set the multiple. A run with no declared budget behaves exactly as today; the production budget is standing configuration and the owner's (G-3). The watchdog stops the wait; whether the provider stops billing an abandoned call is unknown, and the record says so. This implements the second clause of D25. Exhibit: ARCH-20260930-094, where the build judges agreed at $0.070 and the run was killed at 3,600 s having spent $0.51 and returned no answer. Falsifier: a watchdog-ended run whose terminal is written after its budget, or a budgeted run whose stop_reason says the runner killed it, means the watchdog failed; a trip on a fast-judge control run means the pace rule is wrong.'

WHERE: in GraphExecutor, around _run_ai in _execute, so the API path and the eval runner get it identically. The executor takes an optional time budget. The eval runner passes the scenario's declared deadline. engine/workflow.py passes the new optional setting run_time_budget_seconds (default None, meaning today's behaviour), and .env.example gets one commented placeholder line for it. The eval runner's wait_for stays as the outer backstop.

PACE: a tier's pace is the longest completed model-calling step of that tier in THIS run. With no completed step of that tier yet, the call starts and only the mid-flight rule guards it. Record the pace used.

RESERVE: derive it from a measurement, not a guess. Measure, in a test, the time from cancellation to the terminal being written, and set the reserve as a named constant whose comment carries that measurement and the margin, with the arithmetic shown (convention 1). The watchdog must fire before the runner's wait_for, by at least that reserve.

THE APPROVED-ARTIFACT POINTER: 'agreed' means an iteration whose judges agreed (the fold's dissent list is empty, as the adapter's iteration history already records). The watchdog record carries the index of the last agreed iteration, which loop it belonged to, which later gates it passed or did not reach (review, rework_review), and whether the latest implementation differs from it. If there is no agreed iteration, say so explicitly: an absent field and a measured none are different claims (convention 28).

STEP RECORD: the unit record gains steps, a list of {node, iteration, kind, tier, seconds, cancelled} for every executed node, so pace and judging share can be read from the record instead of estimated. Tier as resolve_tier gives it, null for non-model nodes.

SERIALISER REPAIR (instrument repair, found by 094): ResultsLog.record writes regrounding, regrounding_rounds and assumptions_declared, plus the new steps and watchdog blocks. A test writes a unit record through ResultsLog to a temporary file, reads it back as JSON, and asserts every block is present, with zeros or an explicit none when quiet. Prove by breaking: drop one field from the writer and show the test fail.

STATUS SEMANTICS (D23): a watchdog end is the workflow's own terminal. Status is blocked, the reason names the watchdog in a plain sentence, the typed record is on state, and stop_reason stays None. The runner's stop_reason is only for when the runner had to kill the run.

TESTS DRIVE THE REAL PATH (convention 22): use the real GraphExecutor, the real workflows/engineering-rnd.yaml and the real PhaseRunner, with make_mock_client given per-function delays that still bill. Millisecond delays and budgets, with margins wide enough that the suite cannot flake. Cases: (a) no budget gives a path, calls and status identical to today; (b) a judge call longer than the remaining budget is cancelled mid-flight, status is blocked, the rule is 'cancelled', stop_reason is None, and the terminal is written before the budget; (c) after one slow judge call, the next judge call is not started when the remaining time is under the pace, and the client call count proves it; (d) through run_scenario with a scenario timeout, the watchdog fires before the runner's wait_for (stop_reason None); (e) engine/workflow.py with the setting unset behaves as today, and with it set the watchdog is active; (f) a cut after an agreed iteration points at that iteration and labels a differing latest implementation unjudged; (g) the serialiser round trip above. PROVE BY BREAKING: disable the watchdog and show (b) end with the runner's kill (stop_reason deadline). Quote it.
